answer: An agent market allocates paid jobs by lottery, with each identity's odds proportional to funds it locks in escrow for 30 days. Whether agents sell yarrow, authenticate a relic, or appraise a plume, splitting one deposit across a thousand identities gives the attacker no greater total chance of winning. To capture more jobs, the attacker must lock up more capital, bearing its financing cost and losing access to it for the full month.
